title: flag a doc insertion that leaves a paragraph with no blank line after it, which joins the next paragraph

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Tool feedback from the reviewer of ork run ork-20261120-152522-c419 (item S394) found that a doc insertion can leave a paragraph with no blank line after it, so the inserted text joins the next paragraph. Evidence: the proposed paragraph at `docs/dashboard.md:535-536` ran straight into the existing 1-9 key paragraph. Nothing in the repo catches this, and a reviewer has to spot it by eye.

The owner decided how to catch it (adj 665, key `review.doc-paragraph-blank-line-lint`, Jon chose "Diff rule", session 8d711f67, 2026-11-27). A go test in `internal/docscheck` diffs the docs against main and flags an inserted line that touches an unchanged non-blank line, before or after. It skips when git or main is absent. This slice builds that test. S457 built the docs vs `cli_test.go` lint (adj 648) and this is separate from it.

Owner decisions, 2026-11-28: adj 665 (diff against main) and adj 670 (only pure insertions; flag when the first inserted line touches a non-blank line before it or the last touches one after it).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
All tests are in `internal/docscheck/blankline_test.go` (new), package `docscheck`. Until the helpers exist the package does not compile, so every test fails. The line-level tests use an in-memory line slice and the git tests use a temporary repo, so none depend on the real history.
- TestParseInsertionsKeepsPureInsertionHunks: given a `git diff --unified=0` text with a pure-insertion hunk (`@@ -5,0 +6,2 @@`), a one-line insertion (`@@ -8,0 +9 @@`, count defaults to 1), a replacement hunk (`@@ -12 +12 @@`), a pure deletion (`@@ -20,2 +19,0 @@`), a deleted file (`+++ /dev/null`) and a non-`.md` file, `parseInsertions` returns only the two pure insertions of `.md` files, with path and first and last new-file line numbers.
- TestInsertionRunningIntoNextParagraphIsFlagged: the S394 case. Lines `["intro", "", "new a", "new b", "old next"]` with insertion 3-4 return an error that names the path and lines and the unchanged line 5.
- TestInsertionRunningOntoPreviousParagraphIsFlagged: lines `["old prev", "new a", "", "old next"]` with insertion 2-2 return an error that names unchanged line 1.
- TestInsertionKeepingBlankLinesPasses: sub-tests for a block between two blank lines, a block at the start of the file, a block at the end of the file, a whole new file (insertion 1 to N), a block whose first line is blank before a non-blank line, and a block whose last line is blank after a non-blank line. None returns an error.
- TestDocInsertionCheckFlagsAJoinedParagraphInAGitRepo: in `t.TempDir()`, `git init`, commit `docs/a.md` on `main` with `one

two
`, then rewrite it as `one

new
two
` without a commit. `docInsertionErrors(root)` returns one error naming `docs/a.md`, and the same repo with `one

new

two
` returns none. The test skips when `git` is not on PATH.
- TestDocInsertionCheckSkipsWithoutMain: a temporary directory that is not a git repo, and a repo whose only branch is not `main`, make `docInsertionErrors` return a non-empty skip reason and no errors. The test skips when `git` is not on PATH.
- TestDocsInsertionsKeepParagraphsApart: runs `docInsertionErrors` on the repo root (`filepath.Join("..", "..")`). It reports each error with `t.Error` and calls `t.Skip` with the reason when the check skipped. It passes on main itself, where the diff is empty.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Create `internal/docscheck/blankline_test.go` with `// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later` and `package docscheck`. Use only the standard library (`os/exec`, `regexp`, `strconv`, `strings`, `fmt`, `os`, `path/filepath`, `testing`).
2. Add `type insertion struct{ path string; first, last int }`, the new-file line numbers of one run of added lines. Add `parseInsertions(diff string) []insertion`. It reads `+++ b/PATH` lines to get the current file, skips `/dev/null` and any path not ending in `.md`, and reads each `@@ -a[,b] +c[,d] @@` header. It keeps a hunk only when the old count b is `0` and the new count d is at least 1 (d defaults to 1), and returns `first=c`, `last=c+d-1`. Count syntax follows `git diff --unified=0`.
3. Add `checkInsertion(lines []string, ins insertion) error`, where `lines` are the new file's lines. A line is blank when `strings.TrimSpace` is empty. Return an error when the first inserted line is non-blank and line `first-1` exists and is non-blank, or when the last inserted line is non-blank and line `last+1` exists and is non-blank. The message is `PATH:FIRST-LAST: inserted lines touch unchanged line N; put a blank line between paragraphs`, with N the touched line. Which hunks count follows the answer to the Owner needed question.
4. Add `docInsertionErrors(root string) (errs []error, skip string)`. Run `git -C root` through `exec.Command`, with no shell. If `exec.LookPath("git")` fails, return skip `git not found`. If `rev-parse --verify --quiet main` or `merge-base main HEAD` fails, return skip `no main branch` or `no merge base with main`. Run `git -C root diff --unified=0 --no-color --no-ext-diff --no-renames --src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/ BASE -- docs`, with BASE the merge-base, so edits that landed on main after the branch point are not read as deletions. For each insertion from `parseInsertions`, read `root/PATH` and call `checkInsertion`. Return the errors. A diff error other than the skip cases is returned as an error, not a skip.
5. Add the tests listed under Failing tests. Build the temporary repo in the git tests with `git -C DIR -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@example.invalid -c commit.gpgsign=false`, and `init -b main`.
6. Run `TestDocsInsertionsKeepParagraphsApart` against the worktree. It should pass because the worktree's doc diff against main either has no insertion of this kind or this slice adds no doc change. If it reports a hunk in a doc this slice did not edit, stop and ask the owner. Edit no doc, `internal/docscheck/cite_test.go` or `internal/docscheck/cliout_test.go`.
7. Run `go -C /home/jon/code/squalor-xyz/ork vet ./...`, `gofmt -l /home/jon/code/squalor-xyz/ork/internal/docscheck` and `go -C /home/jon/code/squalor-xyz/ork test ./...`. Write the changelog entry with `slicer changelog add S647 --text "..." --root /home/jon/code/squalor-xyz/ork`; do not edit `CHANGELOG.md`.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- Acceptance: a doc insertion whose first or last added line touches an unchanged non-blank line is reported by go test ./internal/docscheck, naming the file, the inserted lines and the touched line. An insertion between blank lines, at the edges of a file, or of a whole new file passes. The check skips, and does not fail, when git or main is absent.
- `go test -run TestParseInsertionsKeepsPureInsertionHunks ./internal/docscheck` exits 0 and runs one test.
- `go test -run TestInsertionRunningIntoNextParagraphIsFlagged ./internal/docscheck` exits 0.
- `go test -run TestInsertionRunningOntoPreviousParagraphIsFlagged ./internal/docscheck` exits 0.
- `go test -run TestInsertionKeepingBlankLinesPasses ./internal/docscheck` exits 0 and runs all six sub-tests.
- `go test -run TestDocInsertionCheckFlagsAJoinedParagraphInAGitRepo ./internal/docscheck` exits 0, or the output says SKIP when git is absent.
- `go test -run TestDocInsertionCheckSkipsWithoutMain ./internal/docscheck` exits 0.
- `go test -run TestDocsInsertionsKeepParagraphsApart ./internal/docscheck` exits 0 (PASS or SKIP).
- `go test ./internal/docscheck` exits 0 and the existing citation and CLI-output tests still pass.
- `go vet ./...` exits 0.
- `gofmt -l .` prints nothing.
- `go test ./...` exits 0.
- `slicer check` exits 0.
